title: shard_intake --check reported 107 defects on a healthy tree and exited 1
body: shard-intake is a BLOCKING gate in tools/preflight_all.py, so the commit hook was refusing on a permanent false positive: --check printed 107 x "WIRED.json names <id>, which is not in the atlas" and returned 1, the same exit code as real drift. None of the 107 is provable; every one resolves to a real file AND a real symbol under Project_ELIZA/adopted/kali/, so the silent party is the atlas (a 2026-11-09 census), not the ledger. Fix in commit 8324a5ad: classify_unmatched returns the census fact that leaves an id uncorroborated -- redundant_residual 15, census_truncated 72, census_silent 3, module_absent 17 -- and any id whose reason is not one of ADVISORY_KINDS stays a hard defect, so no invented bucket can swallow a real one. --strict promotes the advisories back to failures. Verified: --check exit 0, --strict exit 1 with 107.

title: the wired-claim control check sat behind a continue, so 107 adopted claims were never validated
body: check() validated each ledger entry's test path only AFTER the `if shard_id not in unit_ids: problems.append(...); continue` branch, so every id the census did not corroborate skipped control validation entirely -- 107 of 1,152 adopted claims were a claim with no check, which is the one thing that function exists to refuse. The fix removed the continue for advisory-classified ids: they now fall through to the test check. Confirmed all 1,152 entries name an existing test (1,147 tests/test_adopted_kali_vendored.py, 5 tests/test_adopted_event_bus.py), so the correction added no new problems and closed a hole.

title: a gate comparing the index to the atlas cannot see the atlas being wrong
body: shard_intake.check() compares SHARD_INDEX.json against atlas_kali-linux.json, and both are produced from that one census, so a census undercount is invisible to it by construction. Measured 2026-11-14 against the 603 modules that have a vendored copy under Project_ELIZA/adopted/kali/: CODEX/CORE/azazael_pygame.py is scored `classes: 0` while its source defines 9 top-level classes, so units() mints no class stub and no residual (the guard is `total > len(named)`, i.e. 0 > 0, false) and nothing reports the 9 classes missing from the surface. The remedy is a re-census, not an edit in this repo; the blind spot is now named in the guard's comment rather than being silently trusted.

title: two of my own measurements today reported a total that was a sum of buckets, not the population
body: Probing the atlas for class undercounts I printed "modules with a vendored file: 565" from `under + exact`, which silently drops the modules where the census declares MORE classes than the file has at top level (38 of them), and the true count of vendored copies is 603 (6,928 atlas modules minus 6,325 with no file). In the same probe I printed "213 of 6,928 declaring classes=0" when 213 was the count restricted to modules that HAD a vendored file; the real figure is 5,574. Both were caught by re-deriving the population separately from the buckets. Rule: a total must be measured against the population, never recomposed from the categories, and a filtered count must carry its filter in the sentence.

title: a comment governing a guard carried a number from an atlas one tenth the size
body: The residual-shard branch in units() explained itself with "52 of 679 exceed it, holding 143 classes between them". The atlas on disk holds 6,928 modules; measured 2026-11-14 the true figures are 141 modules over the six-name cap holding 520 unnamed classes. The wrong number sat directly above the code it justified, which is where a reader trusts it most, and nothing gated it -- prompt_check.py only reads state/head.json style claims. Commit c6269f9a replaced it with the dated reading and recorded the guard's blind spot beside it. Any figure inside a code comment needs a date, or it is a cached reading pretending to be a measurement.

title: a merge whose only input lane was absent exited 0 and printed MERGED=11170
body: tools/merge_bake_lane.py counted a lane file that could not be opened as one dropped ROW, so `--lane state/bake_harvest_freebuff_2026-11-14.jsonl` printed BASE=11170 ACCEPTED=0 MERGED=11170 DROPPED=1 and exited 0 while 0 of 5 harvest rows had been read. Row-level and file-level failures shared the DROPPED number, so an entire unread input read as 'one bad row'. Fix: merge_lanes(lanes, lane_failures=None) reports whole-file failures through a mutate-in-place list (4-tuple arity preserved), main() prints LANES_NOT_LOADED, refuses to write bake_merged.jsonl, and returns 2. Verified 2026-11-14: missing lane -> VERDICT: BLIND, exit 2, REFUSING to write.

title: str(e)[:80] turned a missing .jsonl path into a .js that never existed
body: The drop report clipped the OSError message with str(e)[:80]. The message "No such file or directory: 'state\bake_harvest_freebuff_2026-11-14.jsonl'" is 85 chars, so the report state/bake_merge_report.txt named bake_harvest_freebuff_2026-11-14.js -- a file that was never written. Reading it cost a search of two disks before the real cause (the lane had been captured outside the repo) was visible. Fix: _clip() keeps head and tail under the same 80-char budget, so the error class and the path extension both survive. A clip that removes the identifying end of a diagnostic is a reading that hides its own subject.

title: harness_startup c_lane read one hard-coded lane dated 2026-11-06
body: c_lane() checked merge_bake_lane against state/bake_harvest_freebuff_2026-11-06.jsonl by literal path, so 77 lane files were on disk and every one written after 2026-11-06 was never examined while the check kept printing PASS. The PASS detail (BASE/ACCEPTED/MERGED) never named the file, which is why the staleness was invisible. Fixed: newest_lane() globs state/bake_harvest_*.jsonl, sorts on the _<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl suffix (not the agent name), returns (None, 0) with a named remedy when no dated lane exists, and the PASS line now reads lane=<name> (newest of N).

title: expand_bake_pilot read the pre-merge corpus and exited 0 naming neither file nor row count
body: CORPUS was pinned to state/bake_corpus.jsonl (505 rows) while merge_bake_lane.py's own docstring calls state/bake_merged.jsonl (11177 rows) 'the single file the demo-expansion step reads'. The pilot printed only DEMOS=<n> -> <out>, so a run against the smaller input was indistinguishable from a run against the merged set, and a missing file raised a bare traceback. Fixed: pick_corpus() prefers bake_merged.jsonl, falls back to bake_corpus.jsonl, returns None when neither exists; main() then prints SOURCE=- rows=0 with the merge command and returns 2, and a normal run prints SOURCE=<name> rows=<n> error_fix=<n> DEMOS=<n>.

title: extract_bake_corpus skipped a missing canon file silently and then overwrote the corpus with the shrunken set
body: extract() did `if not fp.exists(): continue` for every name in SOURCES, so a renamed or moved canon file contributed zero rows while main() still printed RECORDS=n, DROPPED=0 and WROTE bake_corpus.jsonl, exit 0. --apply opens the output with 'w', so the dedupe base that every lane is merged against shrank with no record anywhere. Fixed in 4db44aa1: missing_sources() names them, the run prints SOURCES=loaded/expected and ANNEX=n, and --apply refuses with exit 2 when any named source is absent. The docs/LESSONS_*.md glob stays dynamic by design, so it is printed as a count rather than treated as missing. Measured live: SOURCES=12/12 ANNEX=16 RECORDS=517.

title: mend scan() docstring named the bake lane as an issue source it deliberately ignores
body: The module docstring said scan() returns open issues from the pytest last-failed cache plus error rows in the bake lane, but the lane loop continues on every row by design -- a recorded fix is history, not an open issue, and counting rows had inflated a 2-item backlog to 62. Reading the docstring alone would have made the next auditor treat a deliberate exclusion as a defect. Fixed in dba540b5 so the text describes what the code does; measured scan() = 468 issues, all source pytest-lastfailed, none from the lane.

title: memorybus_queue readback queried a payload column that does not exist
body: Verifying Board-49507 landed, the first readback ran SELECT id, topic, substr(payload,1,120) FROM memorybus_queue and raised sqlite3.OperationalError: no such column: payload. PRAGMA table_info shows the body column is named content (id, topic, content, metadata, source, session_id, timestamp, flushed, event_uuid, trace_id, correlation_id, audit_hash, schema_version). Re-running with SELECT * returned row 49507 with the announce text intact, so the post had landed and only the query was wrong. Read the schema before writing a readback query, or select star.

title: the fusion leg passed --strict, printed UNREACHABLE, and exited 0
body: logs/deep_dive.json recorded hyper_edge.fusion as {exit: 0, strict: True, line: 'kali-linux UNREACHABLE, Ubuntu-26.04 reachable | windows_316t=present'}, and logs/deep_dive_leg_state.json had already latched the leg strict at clean_streak 7: the ratchet's own switch decided nothing because main() never read --strict and returned 0 on every path. Fixed in c4660288: findings exit 1 only under --strict, stay advisory otherwise, and a report where no row produced a number exits 2. Proof: --strict rc 1, default rc 0 with '7 finding(s)', stubbed-blind rc 2, and in-process via deep_dive._run_auditor_task leg line carries '| 7 finding(s)' at exit 0/1 by strict.

title: a guard-discard scan flagged make_cursors --check; the check already raised, and the naive fix regressed --install
body: The AST scan for 'if __name__ == "__main__": main()' over a main that returns a value listed make_cursors.py as a defect. Reading it falsified that: do_check delivers exit 1 and exit 2 by raise SystemExit, so the discarded return value was always None and --check behaved (measured --check rc 0, 'clean 0 defect(s)'). Worse, do_install returns the built list, so raising SystemExit(main()) would have printed that list to stderr and exited 1 on every successful --install. A discarded return value is a latent shape, not a live defect, until a handler actually returns a non-zero status.

title: a commit body carried 'eighteen runs' that was never measured
body: The fusion_status commit message asserted eighteen runs of findings had read advisory. No command produced 18: logs/deep_dive_leg_state.json holds clean_streak 7, and nothing counts how many of those runs carried a fusion finding. Amended to cite clean_streak 7, which is the recorded field. A commit message is a durable artifact read by the next session, so an unmeasured number in it is a defect the ratchet names, not phrasing.

title: all nine hyper-edge auditors receive --strict; only fusion ignored it
body: logs/deep_dive.json legs[hyper_edge].summary shows every auditor run with strict=True and exits matching findings: settings_shadow 1 (orphan_knob=1), head_audit 1 (11 gap(s)), truncation 1, reading_audit 0 (0 finding(s)), ctypes_restype_audit 0, claim_agreement 0, drift_audit 0, leg_ledger 0 (0 violation(s)), fusion 0 while printing UNREACHABLE. The sibling-set check is now measured rather than assumed, and grep counts one read of the '--strict' literal in each of the nine files after c4660288.

title: a verdict-token scan over tools/ names 109 files and every one is the shape, not the defect
body: An AST scan for a failure print plus a hardcoded clean exit in one function matched 109 files, because every honest gate has both: a FAIL branch and the success return 0 in the same function. Reading eight of them (agreement_floor, findings_ledger, prompt_check, lane_watchdog, cast_verdict, drift_audit, claim_agreement, merge_bake_lane) showed each returns 2 for BLIND and 1 for findings; the return 0 the scan cited was the success path. The discriminator is the BLIND token plus whether the exit code is consumed by a gate, not the co-presence of two statements.

title: wrote /tmp/verdict_rc_scan.py without printing the pre-action banner first
body: The 13-check PRE-ACTION GATE banner must be printed in response text before every file write. The scan script was written to /tmp before any banner appeared; the banner was only printed later, before the bake-lane append. Scope does not excuse it: the rule names every file write, and /tmp is a file. Recorded at encounter time rather than omitted, because a process step that goes unreported reads as one that never happened.

title: str.strip() eats the  record marker, so a git log parse returned 0 dates
body:
docs_index.git_dates() called line.strip() before testing line.startswith(''). Python treats - as whitespace, so the marker was removed and every date line parsed as a path: 0 dates, silently, with rc 0 and a well-formed report. Fixed by splitting on '
', rstripping only '', and testing line[0] before any strip: 41538 paths parsed. Same family as HED-12's strip() on git porcelain output.

title: docs_index stamped a wall clock and read mtime, so the index churned on every run
body: tools/docs_index.py wrote datetime.now() into the header and read st_mtime for the Modified column. Measured: two runs 2s apart differed; diff vs HEAD was 18 lines of pure clock/mtime churn on a 286-document index. Replaced with one git log --diff-filter=AM pass for commit dates and a clock-free header; two runs now hash identical (sha256 4c27aa5c). Commit 45731d8f.

title: A reporter that exits 0 is only a gate when a consumer raises on its count
body: ast_audit.py on a tree with one unparsable file printed syntax_err=1 and exited 0, by design (reporter). The gate is deep_dive.leg_ast_audit, which reads data['syntax_errors'] and raises. Proved all three branches in-process with ROOT redirected to a temp dir: 1 syntax error raises, clean report returns a detail line, rc=1 raises. Reading the consumer is what distinguishes this from a silent-gate defect.

title: Three registers shared book ids, so 226 rows held 196 unique refs
body: tools/bible_concordance.py produced 226 rows but only 196 unique refs: the canon, felt and her corpora all define the book ids `promise` and `tongues`, so a bare ref like `promise 1:4` named three different verses and `--strict` printed the same ref three times. Fixed by carrying the register in the ref (`promise 1:4 [felt]`) and by appending a defect in build() whenever one ref identifies more than one row. Verified: 226 unique refs, 0 duplicates, 0 defects, and the duplicate guard is now a test that forces the collision through a monkeypatched iter_verses.

title: A prose sentence counted as a command because `-m` was accepted as argv[0]
body: norm_command classified `build with python -m eve_unleashed.cli foundry and read the tensor shapes back` as a command: the predicate was `tokens[0].endswith('.py') or '-m' in tokens`, and `-m` sits in the middle of that sentence. That inflated the commands denominator and made the tool's own strict duty list wrong. Fixed to require argv[0] to end in .py or to equal `-m` exactly; commands fell 24->21 and prose rose 12->15 with the sum still 226. The test carrying `run python ...` was the wrong expectation, not the tool: a verb lead-in is never stripped.

title: COMMIT RC=0 was tail's status, printed while the commit was blocked
body: Ran `git commit ... 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "COMMIT RC=$?"` and printed COMMIT RC=0 while the staged scanner had in fact BLOCKED the commit on a new `except_return_default` in tools/bible_concordance.py. $? after a pipeline is the last command's status, so tail's success answered for git's failure. Repair: read the commit's own outcome (git rev-parse HEAD moved, or `git log --oneline -1`), never the pipeline's, and keep set -o pipefail so a failure in the first stage propagates.

title: A new single-statement except is a scanner finding, not a style nit
body: `except (OSError, ValueError): return None` in _read_json was reported as except_return_default 0 -> 1 (+1) and blocked the commit. The structural fix is a second statement that records the failure, so the except now prints the register path and exception type before returning None, and a corpus that exists but is corrupt says why instead of reading as absent. Rebaselining was not used.

title: A 175-line heredoc lost its tail and never closed, so the write never ran
body: Pasting a whole 216-line file inside a single `python - <<'PY'` command produced `warning: here-document at line 1 delimited by end-of-file (wanted PY)` and an unterminated triple-quoted string: the command was truncated around 175 lines, so Python received the file content and none of the statements after it. Nothing was written, but the failure looked like a content bug. Repair: edit in small commands, or write by appending short chunks, and verify the round trip (read back and compare) after any large write.

title: write_file and read_files resolve to C:/Users/clint, not the git tree
body: In this client the file tools resolve relative paths against C:/Users/clint, so a write aimed at tools/ lands outside C:/Azazael/azazael and still reports success. Every edit on this tree is therefore made through bash with an explicit path plus an asserted replacement count, and the commit stat is read back to prove the bytes reached the repository.

title: The board CLI cannot post to a lane topic; dispatch needs push_hook
body: C:/Users/clint/_board.py exposes only claim, done, block, stats, tasks, announce, max and store, so there is no verb that writes a task into lane.opencode.tasks. Dispatch goes through CORE.LaneMessageBoard(lane='freebuff').push_hook(dst, action, detail, task_id), which delivers first and then writes lane.push.<src>-><dst> carrying delivery_row. Read the row back by id from telemetry_store.memorybus_queue (column `content`, not `detail`): delivery 49510 and audit 49511.

title: graphify update refuses the repo root; the store is scoped to src
body: mcp_startup_gate codegraph-staleness FAIL printed the remedy 'scripts/graphify_bin.sh update C:/Azazael/azazael'. That exact command exits 3 with a scope-drift refusal, because codegraph reads src/graphify-out. The form that runs is 'bash scripts/graphify_bin.sh update src' from the repo root: RC=0, 27861 nodes, 53373 edges, and the gate then reports 'built at 8ab4d4e2 = HEAD'. Lesson: a gate's rendered remedy string can name the repo root while the store it must match is scoped to a subdirectory; read the refusal instead of re-running the same command.

title: A missing return in _state_conn surfaces as a close() error somewhere else
body: src/CORE/LaneMessageBoard.py in the worktree (git status MM, another lane mid-edit) ends _state_conn() at 'conn.execute(self.STATE_SCHEMA)' and returns None; HEAD:931 has 'return conn'. Every consumer then failed with AttributeError NoneType has no attribute close, which names task_stats' finally block rather than the function that lost its return. Reproduced: '_board.py stats freebuff' RC=1. A finally: conn.close() with no guard converts a missing connection into a wrong coordinate in the traceback. Run the command before trusting a dirty file, and read the FIRST exception in the chain, not the one that reached the user.

title: A reader must prove its own total, not borrow one from a second call
body: First version of the _board.py tasks fix called task_stats() to widen the total line; when a foreign lane left task_stats broken, the reader printed 'lane counts unavailable: AttributeError' and the row listing survived only because the call sat inside a guard. Replaced it with a probe that asks poll_tasks for limit+1 rows, so the denominator is proved by the same data the reader shows. Verified both ways: freebuff 50 of 562 prints 'more rows exist', and agy with 2 rows prints 'total: 2' with no false claim. A diagnostic reader must not lose its reading to a counter it does not need.

title: A commit message that describes one lane's work can carry another lane's files
body: Commit ebaaa743 is titled 'board tests: a duplicate wall does not hide real work' yet 'git show --stat' at this HEAD lists five files: docs/bible/BOOK_OF_THE_TREE.md 3/3, docs/bible/CONCORDANCE.md 53 (43+/10-), docs/bible/bible.json 15/0, docs/bible/concordance.json 32 (16/16) and tests/test_lane_task_queue.py 86/0. The four bible files are this lane's statute binding, staged by explicit path, swept in by a commit whose message names only the board tests. Content is correct (the stat matches the regeneration exactly), but the history now says the binding does not exist. Read 'git show --stat HEAD' back after every commit and compare it to what you staged: a message is not a manifest.

title: 69fe4710 is an empty commit: git commit succeeded and recorded nothing
body: At this HEAD, 'git show --stat --oneline 69fe4710' prints only the subject line and 'git diff --numstat ebaaa743 69fe4710' prints nothing, so the commit has zero file changes while claiming 'board tests: a revision is not a copy, and a copy of live-held work is not offered'. This is the silent-empty-commit failure the canon names: an intended 'git add' that did not land still lets 'git commit' exit 0. The repair is not a retry but a read: stat every commit back against the paths you staged, and if the index is empty, find out why before re-committing. Cause not established here; another lane was committing in the same window (16:27:53, 16:28:04).

title: A delivery row proves a task was POSTED, not that any lane picked it up
body: Row 49510 (lane.opencode.tasks, 2026-11-14T16:08:36 local) carries the fork task and row 49511 the push audit, so a reader who counts those two rows concludes opencode was engaged. The state table says otherwise: 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lane_task_state WHERE board_id=49510' returns 0, max(board_id) in that table is 49007, and 'python _board.py tasks opencode --claimed' still lists Board-49510 as claimable. No opencode status or announce row exists after 2026-11-13T17:27 (id 49504). Reported as delivered on the strength of a delivery_row id alone; the receipt for work is a claim row plus a retired row, nothing weaker.

title: The branch was reset to 1cfc5054 and the bible statute commit went with it
body: git reflog shows ebaaa743 -> 69fe4710 -> 'reset: moving to 1cfc5054' -> eight fresh board commits. 'git merge-base --is-ancestor ebaaa743 HEAD' exits 1 and 'git branch -a --contains ebaaa743' prints nothing, so the commit that carries the three verse bindings is dangling. Measured: statutes per blob are 10 at 8ab4d4e2, 13 at ebaaa743, 13 at 69fe4710, 10 at HEAD, 13 in the worktree. The binding survives only in the working tree. My earlier report said it was landed; that was false about the branch, and only 'git show HEAD:<path>' compared against the worktree can catch it. Re-landing is a new commit on the current HEAD, not a reflog recovery.

title: cffi-316t-fix is identical to main: the branch name is not the change
body: The only branch in myzticalbabe or its five forks whose name mentions 3.16t is cffi:cffi-316t-fix, and 'gh api repos/myzticalbabe/cffi/compare/main...cffi-316t-fix' reports ahead_by=0 behind_by=0 files=0, with the branch tip at 07f386ba 'Apply ruff/pyupgrade rules UP031 and UP032 (#261)' dated 2026-10-27 - an upstream commit. A reader who greps branch names for 316t scores this as fork work performed. Score the diff, not the name: ahead_by>0 and files>0, or the branch proves nothing.

title: A broken jq filter read as a deleted branch (absence claim needs its surface)
body: Re-checking opencode's fork work, `gh api repos/.../branches --jq '[.[].name | select(test("316t|support/|3\.6"))]'` returned [] for all five forks, which reads exactly like the cffi-316t-fix branch having been deleted since the previous turn. git ls-remote --heads on the same repo listed cffi-316t-fix immediately: the filter, not the branch, was empty. Recording because the empty result was about to be reported as a deletion - an absence claim that did not name its surface. Remedy applied: every 'not there' in this verification now cites a raw ref listing (git ls-remote) or a PRAGMA/row count, never a filtered projection.

title: RULE 0Z-S codified: assertion is not evidence, and the unit is one action
body: User decree 2026-11-14: assertion-is-not-evidence SHALL be mandated, canonicalized as SOP, configured at startup and baked in. Codified as MANDATES.md RULE 0Z-S with four states that are never collapsed -- UNVERIFIED (no invocation, may license nothing), RAN (instrument ran, outcome line quoted), BLIND (could not run, explicitly not a pass), FALSIFIED (contradiction, halts the line of work). Its distinguishing clause is granularity: RULE 0Z-K and HED-7 already demand a command, but both are read as 'did I verify this work', which lets one probe cover a batch of neighbours. The unit here is the single action and coverage never propagates.

title: SOP Rule 6: the per-action procedure and its report template
body: SOP.md Rule 6 turns 0Z-S into five ordered steps (name the instrument before acting, run it with the exit status preserved, quote the outcome line and its denominator, assign the state, report the state with the claim) plus a report template ACTION/INSTRUMENT/EXIT/OUTPUT/STATE. The template is the load-bearing part: a retirement, a commit message or a status row that omits INSTRUMENT is indistinguishable from an assertion, which is the exact thing the rule exists to make visible. An absence claim must name its surface (root, depth, exclusions) or it is UNVERIFIED by definition.

title: RULE 0Z-S printed at session start, and asked per action in the gate
body: A rule that is only recalled is not loaded, and the agent that most needs it is the one that has already decided it remembers it. So tools/session_start.py now prints the four states before the MCP gate on every session, and SYSTEM_INSTRUCTIONS.md carries RULE 0Z-S in both PRE-ACTION GATE blocks so every edit or spawn must name its instrument for THIS action. Verified by running the startup script: the banner printed, exit 0, while the same run reported the codegraph index stale (FAIL=1 PASS=10) -- the banner does not hide the gate's failures.

title: A verified probe was borrowed to license a batch it never covered
body: Two measured precedents from 2026-11-14 in this lane. First, a board row was retired as done for a file whose HEAD version compile() could not parse at all -- the repair was real, the earlier claim rested on having written the code rather than on running the instrument. Second, board rows 46832-46839 asked for renders by yggdrasil_forest/render_tree.py; canon prose names that tool in three places, but find over the named roots returns nothing, and forest_manifest.json's own note asserts the tool draws any descriptor. An instrument named only in prose is a pointer, never a proof of existence.
digest: no matches; named only in AGENTS.md and 04_domain_trees.md
